title: Cluster + Pool Utilization Telescope — weekly export
body:
Purpose:
This is a weekly export from the cluster/pool utilization dashboards using the new 'telescope' exporter (iterative view stitched across 7 rolling days). Goal: give infra/product a quick read on where headroom is tightening, which pools show microburst risk, and whether we should trigger redistribution or temporary burst-capacity policies for Dedicated customers.

Notes & context (quick):
- Export window: 2026-04-30 00:00 UTC through 2026-05-06 23:59 UTC (7d rolling).
- Source dashboards: cluster-util-v2, pool-occupancy-ledger, microburst-index-v1.
- Sampling cadence: 5m. Aggregation: per-cluster avg/95/99, per-pool avg/95, node-count live.
- This sheet is intentionally lightweight (no full 1h histograms) — follow-up exports available on demand.

Summary findings (top-of-page):
- NA-east (cluster: nebula-na-e-1) average utilization climbed from 62% -> 78% over the week; 99p spiked to 98% on 2026-05-04 14:40 UTC (sustained ~12m). Microburst index for pool gpu-ai-standard-na peaked at 0.72 (threshold 0.6).
- EU-west clusters remained stable overall (avg 44%), but pool gpu-train-eu has two short sustained 99p events (2026-05-02 and 2026-05-05) aligning with nightly training batch jobs from customer ACME-X (see linked JIRA-1342).
- APAC pool gpu-infer-apac showed low average (31%) but high fragmentation: many small allocations causing slot fragmentation, 18% idle sockets across the pool at 2026-05-06 03:00 UTC.

Per-cluster highlights (relevant rows exported):
- nebula-na-e-1: nodes=48, avg=78%, p95=92%, p99=97.8%, peak-99-duration=12m, microburst-index=0.72, notes="sustained customer-facing latency increase on 5/4; likely KV cache churn"
- comet-na-w-2: nodes=36, avg=51%, p95=67%, p99=80.3%, peak-99-duration=4m, microburst-index=0.34, notes="spiky but short, batching config recommended for low-latency customers"
- orion-eu-w-1: nodes=40, avg=43%, p95=60%, p99=85.2%, peak-99-duration=8m, microburst-index=0.58, notes="training windows at 02:00-04:00 UTC"
- atlas-apac-s-1: nodes=28, avg=31%, p95=45%, p99=63.1%, fragmentation=18%, notes="consider slot compaction/packing policy or tenant coalescing"

Per-pool synthesis and recommended actions:
- gpu-ai-standard-na (pool across nebula-na-e-1 and comet-na-w-2): combined avg=69%, p95=88%, p99=95%
  - Risk: near-production headroom band for on-demand customers. If next-week forecast (based on queued Dedicated reservations) >10% increase, recommend pre-warm burst-capacity (reserve 8 nodes) or enable soft-fallback routing to gpu-ai-spot-na.
- gpu-train-eu: avg=47%, but nightly 99p spikes cause transient queue growth.
  - Action: talk to solutions-eng to shift large batch windows to 04:00-08:00 UTC or enable greedy preemption with lower-priority batch tenants. Ticket: JIRA-1342 (owner: Priya).
- gpu-infer-apac: fragmentation is hurting effective capacity.
  - Action: enable packing policy T2 for small inference jobs, ship a slot-compaction job during low-traffic window (2026-05-09 01:00 UTC).

Microburst and tail-latency correlation notes:
- We observed correlation coefficient ~0.67 between microburst-index and 99p latency across NA clusters this week (sampled at 5m). Suggest adding additional slow-path logs for requests during high microburst windows to debug KV cache eviction patterns.
- Two notable microbursts in nebula-na-e-1 corresponded with a PR merge in model-serving (PR #842) that changed batch padding behavior — linked in artifacts. Recommend rollback test in canary cluster.

Shot-term capacity ops checklist (one-liners):
- [ ] Pre-warm 8x A100-equivalent nodes in NA-east candidate pool (responsible: Miguel).
- [ ] Schedule slot compaction for atlas-apac-s-1 (responsible: Alexandra).
- [ ] Open channel with customer ACME-X to shift training windows (owner: Priya).
- [ ] Run targeted trace capture for nebula-na-e-1 during expected microburst window (5/4 14:00 UTC repeat) — follow SRE tracing runbook.

Metrics export excerpt (sample rows formatted as TSV for quick copy):
cluster	nodes	avg	p95	p99	peak99_dur	microburst_idx	fragmentation
nebula-na-e-1	48	0.78	0.92	0.978	12m	0.72	0.06
comet-na-w-2	36	0.51	0.67	0.803	4m	0.34	0.03
orion-eu-w-1	40	0.43	0.60	0.852	8m	0.58	0.04
atlas-apac-s-1	28	0.31	0.45	0.631	2m	0.21	0.18

Interpretation heuristics used (so reviewers can reproduce):
- avg = 5m-sampled mean across nodes, weighted by node-count.
- p95/p99 = distribution across all sampled request-level utilization measurements (not node-level average).
- microburst-index = (count of >90th-percentile 1m spikes) / (count of 5m windows) normalized by cluster size — threshold 0.6 tuned from historical alerts.
- fragmentation = proportion of idle sockets that are isolated (cannot be coalesced into full allocations) at snapshot time.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want telescope exports to include the 1h histograms by default? It would increase sheet size ~6x but help debugging.
- Is the 0.6 microburst threshold still correct for clusters with <30 nodes? (atlas-apac-s-1 shows low microburst despite high fragmentation).
- Need confirmation from revenue team on ACME-X committed Dedicated windows next quarter (affects whether to pre-warm nodes).

Raw links and evidence references (quick):
- Nebula NA event trace: slack thread #sre-incident (link internal) — see 2026-05-04 14:45 message (Miguel).
- PR changing padding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-serving/pull/842
- JIRA tickets: JIRA-1248 (capacity playbook update), JIRA-1342 (ACME-X training cadence), JIRA-1401 (slot compaction job request).

Appendix: small notes for ops runbook update (if approved):
- Add microburst-index to the daily health check email when >0.55 for NA clusters.
- Automate pre-warm proposal email to oncall and capacity owners when combined pool avg >72% for 48h.

-- end of telescope export --

Notes to reviewers: this is a working export. I left raw TSV excerpt for quick copy/paste into spreadsheet tools. If you want the full per-tenant breakdown, ping and I'll run the tenant-labeled exporter (adds ~120 columns).
